body:
FFmpeg considers `Lossless transparent.webp` to be an invalid file as per `ffprobe` output:

```
Input #0, webp_pipe, from '.\Lossless opaque.webp':
  Duration: N/A, bitrate: N/A
  Stream #0:0: Video: webp, argb, 128x256, 25 fps, 25 tbr, 25 tbn

[webp @ 0000025aa924c980] skipping unsupported chunk: ANIM
[webp @ 0000025aa924c980] skipping unsupported chunk: ANMF
[webp @ 0000025aa924c980] image data not found
[webp_pipe @ 0000025aa921f940] Could not find codec parameters for stream 0 (Video: webp, none): unspecified size
Consider increasing the value for the 'analyzeduration' (0) and 'probesize' (5000000) options
Input #0, webp_pipe, from '.\Lossless transparent.webp':
  Duration: N/A, bitrate: N/A
  Stream #0:0: Video: webp, none, 25 fps, 25 tbr, 25 tbn

Input #0, webp_pipe, from '.\Lossy transparent.webp':
  Duration: N/A, bitrate: N/A
  Stream #0:0: Video: webp, yuva420p(tv, bt470bg/unknown/unknown), 128x256, 25 fps, 25 tbr, 25 tbn
```

I'm guessing Krita does something when using lossless with 100% quality that makes the file nonstandard. The `ANIM` chunk in particular is suspicious, which makes me think the WebP is animated for some reason. (I don't think animated WebP import has been extensively tested, but I would expect it to work with the first frame always being imported.)

Thank you for taking a look, that's helpful to know. I double-checked my export settings. I made sure that 'Save as animated WebP' was disabled, but still received the same decoding error in Godot. At least lowering the quality slider is an easy workaround. Also, someone on the forum said that Godot also can't decode lossless transparent WebP images exported from Aceprite. I've asked if they'd be able to share an example file here. Screenshot of my Krita export settings:

I have the same problem, not lossless, just whatever the default dialogue presents when exporting in Krita. (Quality 75%, Tradeoff 4)

Two files saved exactly the same way, 90b opens, 180b doesn't:

Godot v4.5.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8129) - AMD Ryzen 9 8945HS w/ Radeon 780M Graphics (16 threads) - 31.29 GiB memory

Files in a zip: [bug-report.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22854299/bug-report.zip)

Works:
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec5daf68-e37f-4ac5-b7d7-2adbd1bed6a2)

Doesn't work:
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2320446b-56a7-46b5-ba2e-121d35c47b4b)

I have been encountering this on 4.6 as well, also using Krita. I have even had it happen on some lossy compressed images, not just lossless. Unfortunately I don't have a good example image to share for testing, it seems kind of erratic which do and don't cause the issue. In one case I fixed it by simply changing it from the "default" to "text" compression preset. I will update if I find some consistent way to make an image work or fail.
